Powers Steps

Power supply steps at a glance

Step Main parameters Result / purpose
Power Set Output Channel, Voltage (V)/Current Limit (A), at least one Set voltage or current limit without enabling output.
Power Output ON Channel Enable the selected channel output.
Power Output OFF Channel Disable the selected channel output.
Power Measure Channel Return Voltage and Current without changing settings.
Power Protection Status All or Specific channel Return three protection trip Booleans without clearing protection.

Select the target Powers instance first. Invalid parameters, unsupported model operations or Worker errors fail the step. A reported trip is not itself a failed status step; use the Assert example below if a trip should fail the workflow.

Select a channel

The Channel dropdown is shared by Power Set Output, Power Output ON, Power Output OFF, Power Measure, and the Specific channel selection in Power Protection Status. It lists only channels confirmed by the target instance's capabilities as CH1, CH2, etc. Simulation uses the simulator channels; Live uses the model identified for the saved Resource in Setup. Changing the target instance, Execution Mode, or Powers executable updates the available channels.

Loading, a missing Live model, a failed capability query, or an empty channel list displays a hint and disables fixed channel selection. Saved channels outside the supported list remain visible as unsupported or unconfirmed and are preserved when saving and reloading. Existing Channel bindings are shown as Bound channel (preserved). Selecting a supported fixed channel explicitly replaces the saved channel or its binding; capabilities never change it automatically.

Power Set Output

Add Power Set Output to set a channel's Voltage, Current Limit, or both. Channel is required; at least one of the two setpoints must be selected. Use Set Voltage and Set Current Limit to include or remove each setpoint; unchecking leaves that instrument setting unchanged. The fields show Voltage (V) and Current Limit (A). Power Set Output allows only numeric Fixed value, Variable, or Calculation setpoints. Calculation operands allow only fixed numbers or variables, with Add, Subtract, Multiply, or Divide. Previous step result, Elapsed time, Timestamp, and comparison calculations are unavailable for setpoints. Templates enforce these restrictions. Resolved variables must still be numeric or Powers action validation fails. Current Limit is the power supply output current-limit setpoint, expressed in A, not a forced output current. This step only configures the setpoints. Use Power Output ON separately to enable the output.

Power Output ON / OFF

Select the target Powers instance and a supported Channel. ON enables the output; OFF disables it. Setting voltage or current limit does not enable output. Live operation requires confirmation; check wiring and safety limits first.

Simulation example: Power Set Output → Power Output ON → Power Measure → Power Output OFF. For real hardware, choose settings within equipment limits. Run-level Safe-Off still applies.

Power Measure

Add Power Measure to read the selected channel's actual Voltage (V) and Current (A) once. It uses the fixed Channel dropdown without enabling the output or changing setpoints. After it completes, later Output, Assert, and Calculation steps can select Voltage or Current from its Step Output. The numeric pointers are /data/measurements/voltage and /data/measurements/current. It is foreground-only; readings do not create a Result column unless you add an Output step.

Power Protection Status

Add Power Protection Status to read protection trip state without changing instrument settings. Select All channels or Specific channel and choose from the Channel dropdown. Switching from All to Specific selects the first supported channel. If capabilities are unavailable or contain no channels, Specific is unavailable and All is preserved; existing Specific values remain preserved. The result offers Protection Tripped, Over Voltage Tripped, and Over Current Tripped. Protection Tripped is true when either voltage or current protection has tripped. Powers Tool validates actual model support.

To fail the Workflow after a trip, add an Assert after Power Protection Status. Select Previous step result → Protection Tripped on the left, == as the operator, and Boolean → False on the right. Status alone does not stop the Workflow, clear protection, or modify the power supply.

For IF/ELSE, the three Protection Status result fields are Boolean: true means the corresponding protection has tripped, and false means it has not. Choose Boolean on the other side of the comparison; selecting a result does not change the other operand.
